items.followUp: Name and explain any four layers of the TCP/IP network model.

rubric.why: Identifies the Physical layer and its role in transmitting bits or signals.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the layer and giving its transmission function.

rubric.why: Identifies the Data Link layer and a function such as framing or error detection.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the layer and giving a correct function.

rubric.why: Identifies the Network layer and its routing or addressing function.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the layer and giving a correct function.

rubric.why: Identifies the Transport layer and a function such as reliable or end-to-end delivery.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the layer and giving a correct function.

modelAnswer: The Physical layer transmits raw bits as electrical, optical or radio signals over a communication medium.
The Data Link layer organizes bits into frames and handles communication between directly connected devices.
The Network layer provides logical addressing and selects routes for data packets between networks.
The Transport layer provides end-to-end delivery of data and may ensure reliable transmission.

items.followUp: Explain the difference between software piracy and copyright.

rubric.why: Explains piracy as unauthorized or illegal copying, use or distribution of software.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for a correct explanation; award 1 mark for identifying it as illegal copying only.

rubric.why: Explains copyright as a legal right that protects a creator's work and controls its use or copying.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for explaining both the legal protection and the creator's rights; award 1 mark for identifying it as legal protection only.

modelAnswer: Software piracy is the illegal copying, installation, use or distribution of software without the owner's permission or a valid licence.
Copyright is the legal protection given to the creator of an original work, giving the creator control over its copying, use and distribution.

items.followUp: List five questions you would ask to understand a problem before solving it.

rubric.why: Recognizes the problem and identifies the information supplied and the result required.
rubric.description: Identify the problem, inputs and required output
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the problem and the input/output information.

rubric.why: Identifies the processing needed and the conditions or limitations that must be considered.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the required operations and constraints.

modelAnswer: What is the problem, and what inputs or information are given?
What output or result is required?
What processing or operations are needed to obtain the result?
What conditions or constraints must be followed?
Is there any special case or limitation that must be considered?

items.followUp: What symbol is used to show the start and end of a flowchart?

rubric.why: Identifies the start point as one use of the terminal symbol.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the symbol shows where the flowchart begins.

rubric.why: Identifies the end or stop point as the other use of the terminal symbol.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the symbol shows where the flowchart ends.

modelAnswer: The terminal symbol is used to show the beginning (Start) and the ending (Stop or End) of a flowchart.

items.followUp: Define HTML and state what it is used for.

rubric.why: Identifies a mark-up language as a language that uses tags to mark or describe content.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining it as a language that uses tags or marks to describe content.

rubric.why: Explains that HTML tags describe or organize content on a web page.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it structures or describes web-page content.

modelAnswer: A mark-up language uses tags to mark and describe the structure or presentation of text and other content.
HTML is a mark-up language used to structure content on web pages.

items.followUp: Give one example each of a paired tag and an unpaired tag in HTML.

rubric.why: Names the tag type that has an opening tag and a corresponding closing tag.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming paired or container tags.

rubric.why: Names the tag type that does not require a separate closing tag.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming unpaired or empty tags.

modelAnswer: The two types of HTML tags are paired (container) tags and unpaired (empty) tags.

items.followUp: Convert the binary number 1101₂ into a decimal number, showing the place-value method.

rubric.why: Shows that binary digits are multiplied by successive powers of 2, starting from the right with 2⁰.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for showing the correct powers-of-2 method.

rubric.why: Gives the correct worked example and decimal result for 1011₂.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly evaluating the example to 11₁₀.

modelAnswer: For 1011₂, multiply each digit by its place value, a power of 2, starting with 2⁰ at the right.

items.followUp: Define memory and name its two main types.

rubric.why: Defines memory as a place or unit in which data and instructions are stored.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition referring to storing data or instructions.

rubric.why: Names the two main types of computer memory.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming primary and secondary memory, or equivalent textbook terms.

modelAnswer: Memory is the part of a computer that stores data and instructions for processing or later use.
The two main types of memory are primary memory and secondary memory.
